title: Sum of Numbers With Units Digit K
summary: Given integers num and k, find the smallest set of positive integers where each integer ends in k and their sum equals num.
statement: Given integers num and k, find the smallest set of positive integers where each integer ends in k and their sum equals num. Return the set's size, or -1 if no such set exists. The set may include repeated numbers, and the sum of an empty set is 0.
constraints: Choose any positive integers whose decimal units digit is k; values may repeat.
Return the minimum count whose sum is num, or -1 when impossible.
The empty selection is allowed only when num is zero.
hints: Only the chosen count and k determine the sum units digit.
Try counts one through ten; decimal residues repeat after ten.
A count works when count*k is no greater than num and has the same residue modulo ten.
Any remaining difference is a nonnegative multiple of ten and can be added to one chosen number without changing its units digit.
editorial: Any remaining difference is a nonnegative multiple of ten and can be added to one chosen number without changing its units digit.

tests.explanation: Two valid numbers such as 9 and 49 sum to fifty-eight.
No count can have both a units-digit sum ending in seven and a total at most thirty-seven.
